inclusion.I1: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between PTSD patients and controls
inclusion.I2: Control populations may be healthy individuals or trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD

inclusion.I3: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between PTSD patients and controls
inclusion.I4: Whole-brain evidence- The paper must report at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume
inclusion.I5: It is acceptable for qualifying results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials when the main text clearly indicates those results are available.
inclusion.I6: Control populations may be healthy individuals or trauma-exposed individuals without PTS
inclusion.I7: Sample- results must be reported among ADULT humans. The PTSD group and the control group must both be adults (roughly 18 years and older). A sample described as adult, as veterans, or with a reported mean or minimum age of 18 or above qualifies. Do not exclude an otherwise qualifying adult study merely because the full text omits an explicit age range.

exclusion.E4: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results.
exclusion.E5: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human structural MRI data.
exclusion.E6: Sample- paediatric, child or adolescent studies. Exclude when the PTSD group is explicitly described as children, youths, adolescents or paediatric, or when its reported age range lies wholly or mostly below 18 years. This source meta-analysis restricted itself to adult humans.
exclusion.E7: Morphometry performed by NON-VOXEL-BASED methods only- surface-based or vertex-wise cortical thickness, FreeSurfer cortical or subcortical parcellation volumes, shape/vertex analyses, or tensor-based morphometry, where no voxel-based (VBM) whole-brain grey-matter contrast is also reported. The source meta-analysis excludes "other non-voxel-based morphometry methods" deliberately.
exclusion.E8: Studies about trauma or stressful life event studies not specifically measuring PTSD
exclusion.E9: Treatment and longitudinal studies without a qualifying between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls
exclusion.E10: Studies that report only within group results in PTSD patients without a qualifying between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls
exclusion.E11: Studies report only null results (i.e., no significant differences between PTSD patients and controls)

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Must be a voxelwise whole brain analysis of grey matter volume

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: Region of interest (ROI) or small volume correction (SVC) analyses
exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Analyses of other modalities (e.g., functional MRI, diffusion tensor imaging) or other structural measures
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Within group analyses that do not compare PTSD patients to controls
exclusion.GLOBAL_E4: Analyses of treatment effects or longitudinal changes

inclusion.INCREASED_GM_I1: Voxelwise whole-brain grey matter comparison between PTSD patients and controls, with a patients > controls contrast indicating increased grey matter in PTSD patients.

inclusion.DECREASED_GM_I1: Voxelwise whole-brain grey matter comparison between PTSD patients and controls, with a patients < controls contrast indicating reduced grey matter in PTSD patients.
